note:
Follow-up to banner-lab-glassware-graphite. Malcolm's picks from that wave, 2026-08-25:
  lab-glass--A-cluster-type-left    flux2_01, nbp_flash_02
  lab-glass--C-blue-accent-type-left  nbp_flash_02
All three are the CLUSTER framing, so this batch builds on that and drops the macro-rim framing entirely.

WHAT CHANGES: the glassware now carries three liquids in the products' own colours — blue, rose-pink and water-clear — rather than one accent colour or none. Blue is the palette's Clinical blue 014EB1, the Copper Peptide scene colour; rose-pink is Blush F3BFC2, the PDRN scene colour; the third vessel is left water-clear for the frosted-white products, Acetyl Hexapeptide-8, Matrixyl and Glutathione. Using the agreed scene colours rather than invented ones is what keeps these bands in the same world as the product photography.

The colours are assigned to SPECIFIC vessels in each brief rather than left to the engine, because 'three different coloured liquids' without assignment produced inconsistent pairings across suppliers on the earlier wave.

CLASS B: no product, no branding, no references, FLUX.2 in the run.

DIGITS STAY IN THE NEGATIVES and are worth keeping there. FLUX.2 rendered printed graduation markings on both previous waves — '100 / 50 / 10' and '500 ml' — and is the only engine that does. Treat it as a trait of that backend rather than something a stronger negative fixes; its candidates need checking at full size before use.

MALCOLM'S PICKS FROM THIS WAVE, 2026-08-25:
  lab-colours--A-cluster-type-left   nbp_flash_02
  lab-colours--C-cluster-type-right  nbp_flash_02
Noted rather than renamed: manifest.json references these paths, and renaming is how marks have been lost on this project before.
Caveat on the A pick: nbp_flash_02 is one of the two candidates that SWAPPED the assignment - pink beaker on the left, blue flask centre, rather than blue flask then pink beaker. It reads well on its own; it just will not match the rest of the wave if several are used together.

slots.title: lab colours — A · cluster of three, blue / pink / clear, type zone left
slots.prompt:
Close-up laboratory photograph. Three pieces of clear borosilicate glassware stand together on a dark bench in the right half of the frame, between 55 and 92 percent of frame width, close to camera and the sharpest thing in the picture.

Each holds a different liquid, filled about two thirds, perfectly still with a crisp meniscus, and the colours are assigned as follows and must not be swapped: the conical Erlenmeyer flask holds a clear vivid BLUE liquid, colour hex 014EB1; the low cylindrical beaker beside it holds a clear ROSE-PINK liquid, colour hex F3BFC2; the tall narrow test tube in a simple stand holds a WATER-CLEAR colourless liquid. No other colour appears anywhere in the frame.

The key light passes through the blue and the pink so both glow from within and pool a little of their own colour onto the bench beneath them; the clear tube stays colourless and reads as bright glass.

Behind the group a working laboratory reduced to shape and light: matte black instrument housings, a chrome stand, the curve of a larger apparatus, all thrown far out of focus at f/2 so nothing on them is identifiable and no surface is readable. The bench and ground are deep graphite, colour hex 1A1A1A, falling away to near black at the frame edges.

One hard key light from the upper left rakes across the glass, drawing bright edges down each vessel and laying hard-edged shadows to the right; one soft fill only. The left 42 percent of the frame, measured from 0 to 42 percent of frame width, is empty defocused bench held at even tone and low detail so a headline can sit on it unaided. Shot on a 50mm, clinical, cold, precise, no styling props.
slots.negative_extra: no glassware overlapping confusingly, no spillage, no droplets on the bench, no cork or rubber stopper, no stirring rod, no colour mixing, no gradient inside a single vessel

slots.title: lab colours — B · stepped line receding, blue / pink / clear, type zone left
slots.prompt:
Close-up laboratory photograph, shot low and close. Three pieces of clear borosilicate glassware stand in a stepped diagonal line receding away from the camera on a dark bench, the nearest at about 58 percent of frame width and the furthest at about 90 percent.

Each holds a different liquid, filled about two thirds, still and clean with a crisp meniscus, assigned as follows and not to be swapped: the NEAREST vessel is a low cylindrical beaker holding a clear vivid BLUE liquid, colour hex 014EB1, and it is the sharpest thing in the picture; behind it a conical Erlenmeyer flask holding a clear ROSE-PINK liquid, colour hex F3BFC2, slightly softer; furthest away a tall narrow test tube in a stand holding a WATER-CLEAR colourless liquid, softest of the three. No other colour appears anywhere in the frame.

Light passes through the blue and the pink so each glows from within and lays a small pool of its own colour on the bench; the clear tube stays colourless.

Behind them a working laboratory reduced to shape and specular only: matte black instrument housings and chrome stands thrown far out of focus at f/2, nothing identifiable or readable. The bench and ground are deep graphite, colour hex 1A1A1A, falling to near black.

One hard key light from the upper left rakes along the line of glass, each vessel throwing its own hard shadow to the right. The left 45 percent of the frame, measured from 0 to 45 percent of frame width, is empty defocused bench held at even tone and low detail so a headline can sit on it unaided. Shot at f/4 so the recession is real, clinical, cold.
slots.negative_extra: no even front-to-back spacing, no fourth vessel, no spillage, no droplets on the bench, no cork or rubber stopper, no stirring rod, no colour mixing
